NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

Kenya’s people belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be

able to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by

resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect which enable them to live together in harmony and foster

patriotism in order to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth

progress of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution following in the wake of

rapid modernization. Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and

relevant domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya

recognizes the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part

of this development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our

young people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

ii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instill in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will

lead to physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It

should lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iii

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/

pre-career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners

exiting this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of

the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The

learner will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior

School career teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Agriculture is the Science and art of growing crops and raising animals for food, fiber, medicinal extracts, among other products

and services with the aim of sustaining human life. Its inclusion in the school curriculum is anchored on the United Nations

Sustainable Development Goal number 2 on zero hunger. Learners taking Agriculture in Senior school will build on the

agricultural competencies attained in Junior School. The Agriculture curriculum targets development of competencies in crop

production, animal production, agricultural technologies and entrepreneurship applicable in varied social-economic and

environmental contexts.

The curriculum will be implemented through learner-centered pedagogies such as experiential learning, collaborative learning,

cooperative learning, problem-based learning and project based learning. The curriculum prepares the learner for agricultural

related education and training in middle level colleges and university for career development. The acquired skills will also be

applied in life-long contexts to address food and nutrition security, employment, environmental conservation and mitigation of

climate change.

The curriculum forms foundation for learners to pursue careers in farm management, agri-business management, horticulture,

agricultural economics, agricultural engineering, agriculture biotechnology, agriculture education and extension, agronomy, soil

science, plant science, and animal science related careers such as animal health, veterinary medicine, animal production and food

and dairy technology. Additionally, the learner has an opportunity to develop skills for entrepreneurship in agriculture value

chain.

vii

GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. Apply agricultural principles in logical and critical thinking skills to solve contextual challenges in the society.

2. Apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve contemporary agricultural problems.

3. Employ individual talents to utilise agricultural resources for leisure, career and economic growth, further education and

training.

4. Use ICT and production technologies effectively in varied agricultural processes.

5. Apply and promote healthy interventions in environmental care through agricultural practices.

6. Protect, preserve and improve the environment for agriculture and socio-economic sustainability.

7. Manage pertinent and contemporary challenges responsibly through agriculture and environmental interventions.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able

to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by resolving

conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony and foster patriotism, and make a positive

contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships necessary for the smooth progress of a

rapidly developing modern economy. Rapid modernisation is bound to lead to a silent social revolution, and education should

assist our youth in adapting to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities required to support a growing

economy. Kenya is building a modern and independent economy that needs an adequate and relevant domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognises the

rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only contribute to this development

if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young people for these

changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfillment

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to develop

their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

ii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral values

and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equality and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system that provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and corporate

social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instill in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary society.

Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid development to build

a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations. Education

should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the obligations and

responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to physical or

mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should lead the youth of

Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iii

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre-

career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Computer Studies focuses on the study of computers and computational systems. As learners transition from Junior School to

Senior School, they build upon the foundational knowledge and skills acquired in Pre-Technical Studies in Grades 7, 8, and 9. In

Junior School, learners explored core computer concepts such as computer hardware, software, data safety, ICT tools, and visual

programming. These concepts introduced them to essential digital literacy and basic programming skills while nurturing their

curiosity about computational systems. The emphasis was on fostering an understanding of how computers work and ensuring

learners developed the ability to use technology effectively and safely in everyday contexts.

In Senior School, Computer Studies prepare learners to advance their knowledge and skills in programming, computer networking,

cybersecurity, robotics, and artificial intelligence through coding exercises, software development projects, and networking

simulations. The curriculum employs learner-centered, experiential, and inquiry-based learning methods that emphasise hands-on

activities. These approaches enhance critical thinking and problem-solving skills while promoting innovation and ethical decision-

making in the use of technology.

Computer Studies opens the door to a wide range of career opportunities by equipping learners with knowledge and skills in

computer systems and their applications. Learners can pursue professions in software engineering, data science, cybersecurity,

artificial intelligence, robotics, and IT consultancy, among others. The subject lays a strong foundation for those aiming to further

their studies in Computer Science or related disciplines, empowering them to contribute meaningfully to national development

and thrive in a rapidly evolving digital economy.

vii

GENERAL SUBJECT LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

a) apply the knowledge and skills acquired in Computer Studies to perform daily life activities,

b) practise ethical and safe use of computer technology in society,

c) develop computer applications for solving real-world problems,

d) configure and manage computer networks for effective resource sharing,

e) exploit career and entrepreneurship opportunities in the field of computer science,

f) adapt to the dynamic digital world to cope with the changing societal needs.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

Kenya’s people belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able

to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by

resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect which enable them to live together in harmony and foster

patriotism in order to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution following the wake of rapid

modernisation. Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and

relevant domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognises

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will

lead to physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation.

It should lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre-

career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

a) Apply knowledge on food and nutrition to prevent and manage nutritional deficiency diseases and disorders for healthy

living.

b) Utilise knowledge, skills and attitudes in meal planning, preparation, and service of food for leisure, self-fulfillment and

entrepreneurship.

c) Develop skills for proper care of the home, care and maintenance of clothes and household articles in day-to-day life.

d) Apply principles of consumer education for personal and family financial management.

e) Choose fabrics for various uses based on their different characteristics.

f) Apply various techniques in drafting and grading basic pattern blocks for constructing garments.

g) Construct garments using various clothing construction techniques.

h) Appreciate Home science as a subject and the role it plays in improving the life of an individual, family and the nation.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

Kenya’s people belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able to

live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by resolving

conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect which enable them to live together in harmony and foster patriotism in order

to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress of a

rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution following in the wake of rapid modernization.

Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to support a

growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and relevant domestic

workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes the

rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this development

if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young people for these

changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfillment

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to develop

their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral values

and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and corporate

social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instill in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary society.

Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid development in order

to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations. Education

should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the obligations and

responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to

physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should lead the

youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre-

career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Information and Communication Technology (ICT) is concerned with the use of computers and telecommunication systems to

acquire, create, store, process and disseminate data and information for the purpose of supporting decision making at individual

or organisational level. ICT subject at Senior School builds on the Pre-Technical Studies competencies developed at Junior School

where learners acquired basic skills of computer hardware, computer software, safety, communication and visual programming.

The curriculum aims at equipping all learners at senior school with knowledge, skills, attitudes and values for creative and

innovative use of ICT. It focuses on developing and imparting ICT skills as well as preparing learners who can safely, securely,

socially and ethically use: ICT systems, ICT productivity tools, ICT applications and Internet & web technologies. These

components aim to develop critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, innovation, communication and digital literacy skills, all

considered essential to prepare learners for further studies in higher level of education.

A learner skilled in productivity tools, web development, and basic AI visualization and robotics can pursue careers in digital

media, interactive design, or educational technology. This versatile skill set enables roles like web designer, multimedia artist,

UI/UX designer, or robotics programmer to create engaging websites, visuals, and smart systems.

This subject is anchored on Kenya’s National Goals of Education No. 2, Kenya Vision 2030, and Sessional Paper No. 1 of 2019

by promoting technical skills and innovation. It aligns with the National ICT Policy of Kenya (2016, revised 2020), emphasising

ICT’s role in economic growth.

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

a) Communicate effectively through the use of information and communication technological innovations.

b) Demonstrate knowledge of information and communication technology applications that enhances their personal and

professional productivity

c) Recognise potential risks associated with the use of ICT and means by which they can mitigate the risks in a responsible way.

d) Make valuable contributions to the social and economic development of the society through the use of information and

communication technology skills.

e) Apply knowledge, skills, attitude and values in information and communication technologies in daily live activities and lifelong

learning.

f) Demonstrate information and communications skills that can impact current and new methods of working in the outside world

and on social, economic, ethical and moral issues.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Fine Arts is a creative subject focused on the expression of ideas, emotions, and imagination through various art techniques applied

in both two-dimensional and three-dimensional artworks. These works are created primarily for their aesthetic, emotional impact,

and for functional purposes. Learners entering this level bring foundational knowledge and skills gained from early exposure to

various artistic activities and environments. This subject builds on that base, providing a seamless continuum of learning that

promotes deeper creativity and cognitive development.

The learning process integrates both conventional and digital approaches, emphasizing hands-on techniques, in-depth research,

and exploration of artistic traditions across different cultures. This broad exposure nurtures holistic, globally conscious learners

who appreciate diverse artistic expressions, promote cultural preservation, and contribute meaningfully to modern society.

Aligned with global education trends, learners will leverage ICT tools for innovative experiences in digital art creation, enhancing

both artistic production and digital literacy skills essential in today’s creative industries. The subject lays a strong foundation for

continued growth in art and academics and opens pathways to diverse careers including fine art, architecture, advertising, visual

communication, industrial and product design, interior and fashion design, landscape design, graphic design, urban planning,

photojournalism, medical illustration, animation, video production, curation, and art education.

viii

GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR FINE ART

By the end of senior secondary school, the learner should be able to;

1. Deepen visual perception skills through exploration of various artistic techniques in 2-Dimensional and 3-Dimensional

artworks.

2. Promote understanding of diverse fine art works from Kenya to promote patriotism.

3. Demonstrate appreciation of the Fine art through the historical perspective

4. Acquire research and analytical skills to document and critique artworks.

5. Explore a range of materials, techniques and tools used in fine arts to create functional and aesthetic artworks.

6. Explore and develop skills in ICT for design, production and presentation of fine artworks.

7. Apply creative and innovative skills to make materials from upcycled and recycled objects from the immediate environment.

8. Demonstrate understanding of the creative process in fine arts for portfolio development. (document)

9. Apply entrepreneurial skills for economic empowerment.

10. Appreciate diverse indigenous Kenyan and African crafts for cultural preservation and heritage.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

Kenya’s people belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able to

live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by resolving

conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect which enable them to live together in harmony and foster patriotism in order

to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress of a

rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution following in the wake of rapid modernization.

Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to support a

growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and relevant domestic

workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes the

rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this development

if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young people for these

changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to develop

their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

ii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral values

and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and corporate

social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary society.

Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid development in order

to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations. Education

should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the obligations and

responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to

physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should lead the

youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iii

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre-

career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Music and Dance play a vital role in the holistic development of learners, engaging the cognitive, affective, and psychomotor

domains to foster balanced growth. At the Senior School level, this learning area builds upon the foundational knowledge, skills,

attitudes, and values acquired at lower levels. Learners will deepen their understanding of rhythm, melody, movement, and

expression while exploring diverse genres and styles. The focus will be on nurturing creativity, emotional intelligence, critical

thinking, and cultural awareness through a curriculum that blends theoretical knowledge with practical experience.

Learning in Music and Dance will be experiential, participatory, and learner-centered, designed to prepare learners for lifelong

engagement with the arts and readiness for further education. Learners will be immersed in creating, performing, and appreciating

Music and Dance from Kenyan and global cultures. Through this process, they will develop artistic sensibility, discipline,

collaboration skills, and an appreciation for cultural diversity. The curriculum also supports personal growth, autonomy, and the

development of essential life skills such as communication, confidence, and physical well-being.

Studying Music and Dance opens diverse career pathways within the expanding creative economy. Learners will be equipped to

pursue professions in education, choreography, composition, directing, event organisation, arts management, music production

and technology, sound engineering, music journalism, and music therapy. This makes Music and Dance not only a rich academic

pursuit but also a practical foundation for a wide range of fulfilling and economically viable careers.

vii

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. Apply relevant knowledge, skills, values and attitudes, to create, perform and analyse Music and Dance.

2. Perform Music and Dance from various cultures for self and cultural expression, and preservation.

3. Use available technologies to enhance learning and develop creativity in Music and Dance.

4. Apply research and innovation skills in the sustainable utilisation of locally available resources for Music and Dance creation,

performance and appreciation.

5. Relate Music and Dance to other arts and non-art disciplines to make meaningful connections.

6. Promote cultural, national, moral and religious values through Music and Dance.

7. Foster responsive and responsible global citizenship through involvement in Music and Dance activities from diverse

cultures.

8. Utilise individual potential in Music and Dance for leisure, self-fulfilment, further education and training, and career growth.

9. Address pertinent and contemporary issues in society through Music and Dance activities.

10. Appreciate diverse local and global cultures through listening, analysis and performance of Music and Dance.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must

be able to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood

by resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony and foster patriotism, and

make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships necessary for the smooth progress of a

rapidly developing modern economy. Rapid modernisation is bound to lead to a silent social revolution, and education should

assist our youth in adapting to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities required to support a

growing economy. Kenya is building a modern and independent economy that needs an adequate and relevant domestic

workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognises

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only contribute to this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfillment

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

ii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equality and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system that provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instill in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to

physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should

lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iii

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre-

career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Creative Arts and Sports in Junior School lays a strong foundation for lifelong physical activity by developing learners’ basic

motor skills, introducing them to games, athletics, swimming, physical fitness components, and fostering teamwork and cultural

appreciation through indigenous games. As learners progress to Senior School, Physical Education builds upon these foundational

experiences by enhancing their knowledge, refining physical abilities and strengthening socio-emotional competencies that support

a healthy lifestyle and overall well-being. At this stage, learners gain a deeper understanding of sportsmanship, embrace the

principles of clean and ethical sport and develop essential life skills such as effective communication, teamwork and responsible

decision-making.

In Senior School, the learning of Physical Education will be undertaken through a learner-centered, practical, and experiential

approach that emphasizes active participation, inquiry-based learning, and collaborative activities. Key pedagogies will include

demonstration and practice, peer teaching, project-based learning and outdoor experiential learning, ensuring that learners not only

acquire advanced motor skills but also develop critical thinking, communication, leadership, and problem-solving abilities. The

curriculum is designed to refine learners' physical competencies across various areas including games, athletics, swimming and

outdoor adventure activities. By integrating values such as discipline, integrity, resilience, teamwork and environmental

responsibility, learners will be well-equipped to transition into university and tertiary colleges, or directly into the world of work.

Physical Education offers diverse career opportunities across various fields including PE teaching, coaching, fitness training, and

recreational facilitation, physiotherapy, kinesiology, professional coaching and sports management. There is also a growing

demand in areas such as youth development, sports journalism, talent identification and community sports programs.

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. Exhibit appropriate physical activity skills to prevent or manage challenges related to personal health.

2. Participate actively in physical activities within and beyond the school setting to build knowledge, skills and positive

attitudes in Physical Education.

3. Use technology effectively to support learning and enhance the mastery of skills in Physical Education.

4. Explore and nurture individual talents and abilities for personal growth and fulfillment through Physical Education.

5. Demonstrate environmental responsibility while taking part in physical activities.

6. Display positive behaviour and commitment towards the improvement of personal life, the community, the nation and the

global society.

7. Appreciate and respect individual differences while engaging in physical activities.

8. Apply self-management, interpersonal and decision-making skills through participation in physical activities.

9. Display positive attitudes and uphold values that address pertinent and contemporary issues through involvement in physical

activities.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

Kenya’s people belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able

to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by

resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect which enable them to live together in harmony and foster

patriotism in order to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution following in the wake of rapid

modernization. Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and

relevant domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will

lead to physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It

should lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre-

career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Sports and Recreation is a multidisciplinary field that encompasses the study and understanding of physical activity and its

influence on sports performance, fitness, recreation, and overall wellness. This learning area is designed to provide learners with

the opportunity to explore and actualise their interests in specific sports and games. By engaging in this field, learners gain

comprehensive knowledge and practical skills in various aspects of; physical fitness, recreation activities, coaching, and officiating

in specific games and athletics.

The curriculum covers topics in health and fitness, coaching, and officiating. Learners in this track will develop an in-depth

understanding of how different physical activities impact the body, mind, and social well-being. They will learn how to optimize

performance, prevent injuries, and promote long-term health through regular exercise and balanced living. This holistic approach

ensures that learners appreciate the balance between physical exertion and recovery, fostering a lifelong commitment to healthy

living.

Overall, Sports and Recreation not only prepares individuals for professional careers but also cultivates a culture of health,

wellness, and active living that benefits individuals and society as a whole. After senior secondary school, the learner will have an

opportunity to advance into a specific career in sports or pursue further studies at the tertiary level.

viii

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of senior school, the learner should be able to:

1. utilise technology to effectively create, analyse, store data, and communicate in sports and recreation,

2. conduct scientific inquiry in sports and recreation for problem solving,

3. undertake analysis in sports and recreation in order to interpret data and apply in different sports contexts,

4. demonstrate refined skills and techniques in sports for enjoyment, personal development and career growth,

5. integrate ethical principles and values in physical activities for health and wellbeing,

6. display abilities and competencies to organise, administer and manage different sports and recreation activities for

promotion of healthy lifestyle,

7. utilise sports and recreation programmes for environmental conservation and sustainability,

8. exhibit appreciation of local and global cultural diversity through sports for harmonious co-existence,

9. apply knowledge and understanding of pertinent and contemporary issues in sports and recreation programmes.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

Kenya’s people belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able

to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by

resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect which enable them to live together in harmony and foster

patriotism in order to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution following in the wake of rapid

modernization. Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and

relevant domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

ii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will

lead to physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It

should lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iii

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre-

career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

As learners move from Junior School to Senior School, the study of Theatre and Film becomes more structured, practical and

learner-centered. Building on general exposure to creative and performing arts, already established at Junior School, the Senior

School curriculum focuses on deepening learners' knowledge, technical skills, and appreciation for Kenya’s rich cultural heritage

Through the strands of Creating, Production, and Film, Theatre and Society, the learner engages in creative writing, performance,

directing, adaptation of narratives and cultural expression. The curriculum draws directly from Article 11 of the Constitution,

integrating national values and indigenous knowledge into artistic learning, thus aligning learner creative growth with Kenya’s

socio-cultural identity.

Theatre and Film learning is experiential, reflective, and progressive across the three years of Senior School. In Grade 10, the

learner concentrates on theatre—developing skills in acting, staging, and dramatic writing. In Grade 11, the focus shifts to film,

where the learner explores cinematic storytelling, filming techniques, and editing. Grade 12 integrates both domains, allowing the

learner to refine and showcase their artistic abilities in capstone projects. Assessments are largely performance-based and

formative, encouraging creativity, collaboration and critical thinking. By applying inquiry-based learning, participatory

methodologies, and community-linked projects, the curriculum equips learners with the competencies and mindset needed to

transition into higher education, professional creative practice, or entrepreneurial ventures within the arts sector.

Anchored in the CBC’s emphasis on talent development and career readiness, Theatre and Film supports diverse professional

pathways within Kenya’s creative economy. The learner is introduced to careers such as acting, directing, screenwriting, stage and

set design, cinematography, sound and video editing, and arts production. As the curriculum integrates entrepreneurship and arts

management, it prepares the learner to commercialize their creative skills and manage artistic enterprises. This aligns with Kenya’s

national agenda to promote the creative industry as a pillar of economic growth. With competencies acquired through the CBC,

learners are empowered not only to participate in cultural production but also to innovate and lead within both local and global

creative ecosystems.

This curriculum is meticulously structured to facilitate a progressive learning experience, wherein learners study and engage with

Theatre in Grade 10 and Film in Grade 11, subsequently allowing them the opportunity to specialise and hone their skills in Grade

12. This design thoughtfully considers the allocation of time, resources, and the development of expertise.

vii

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1) Create original, workshopped or adapted theatre and film productions grounded in Kenyan cultures to promote nationalism,

patriotism and national unity.

2) Perform in theatre and film productions for individual development, self-expression and cultural integration.

3) Deploy technology to create theatre and film performances to promote social and economic empowerment for national

development.

4) Use theatre and film as instruments of promoting moral and religious values.

5) Appraise theatre and film performances for self-improvement and problem solving in society.

6) Use theatre and film to promote good health and environmental conservation.

7) Appreciate the role of theatre and film in promoting international cooperation and global citizenship.

8) Employ theatre and film as a means of promoting social equality and responsibility.

9) Apply theatre and film skills to address Pertinent and Contemporary Issues in society.
