NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must

be able to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood

by resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony and foster patriotism, and

make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships that are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. In the wake of rapid modernisation, there is bound to be a silent social revolution.

Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities required to support a

growing economy. Kenya is building a modern and independent economy that needs an adequate and relevant domestic

workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognises

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iv

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equality and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system that provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to

physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should

lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

v

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre-

career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Media Technology in the Senior School curriculum builds upon foundational competencies developed in Junior School Pre-Technical Studies,

with an expanded focus on the dynamic interplay between media, information, communication, and the digital economy. Learners transition

from general exposure to technological tools to a more specialized engagement with content creation, media production, and immersive digital

environments. The subject introduces them to interactive platforms, emerging technologies, digital storytelling, and media entrepreneurship.

Rooted in the principles of the National ICT Policy (2019) and aligned with the UNESCO 2030 Sustainable Development Goals, the

curriculum emphasizes ethical digital citizenship, innovation, and critical engagement with media as both a tool and a transformative force in

society.

Learning in Media Technology is experiential and inquiry-based, with a strong emphasis on hands-on activities, project-based learning,

collaboration, and research. Learners are guided to think critically, work innovatively, and apply digital tools across various media formats.

They engage with real-world scenarios through simulations, prototyping, and problem-solving tasks that foster analytical and entrepreneurial

skills. Through iterative production processes and peer review, learners develop fluency in managing content, mastering digital tools, and

adapting to technological shifts. The progression of learning equips them with the competencies required for further education and for

responding to the evolving demands of the 21st-century knowledge economy.

Media Technology prepares learners for a broad spectrum of careers within the creative, digital, and communication sectors. Potential

pathways include digital content creation, film and television production, multimedia design, animation, journalism, advertising, game design,

virtual and augmented reality development, media research, and digital marketing. The subject also nurtures entrepreneurial capacity, enabling

learners to innovate within the digital economy and contribute meaningfully to Kenya’s creative industries and global media landscape. The

subject cultivates a generation of innovative, digitally literate, ethically grounded, and technologically adept industry-ready professionals

equipped to drive progress in their higher education and in the creative and digital industries both locally and globally.

ix

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. Effectively communicate with media technologies in promoting the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for

national development.

2. Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills while using media technologies.

3. Employ technical skills in media technology to carry out fundamental research.

4. Develop individual creativity and digital competencies for personal fulfilment, career development, further education and

training.

5. Demonstrate ethical practices in media production and consumption.

6. Utilise media literacy skills to promote public health and conservation of the environment towards sustainable development.

7. Engage in local and international media as part of bringing about positive social change and coexistence in society.

8. Appreciate cultures and global outlook represented through media with respect.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

Kenya’s people belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able

to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by

resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect which enable them to live together in harmony and foster

patriotism in order to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution following in the wake of rapid

modernization. Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and

relevant domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

ii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instill in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will

lead to physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It

should lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iii

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre-

career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Metalwork is one of the subjects in the Technical Studies track of the Science Technology Engineering Mathematics (STEM)

pathway. It builds on the competencies acquired in Pre-Technical Studies, Integrated Science and other related learning areas at

Junior School. Metalwork equips the learner with exploration, imagination, creativity, innovation and hands-on skills through

practical activities, field trips and projects.

The strands include; Fundamentals of Metalwork, Tools and Materials, Related Drawing and Metal Joining and Finishing

processes. These strands aim to develop critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, innovation, communication, digital literacy,

and practical skills all considered essential in both personal life and the world of work. The subject delivery emphasizes the use

of learner centered approaches through varied facilitation, learning experiences and resources. This approach entails both theory

and practice, distributed uniformly throughout the subject. The content is developed from basic science and technology concepts

to more advanced application concepts based on the developmental level of the learner.

Metalwork is anchored on National Goals of Education No. 2 on providing the learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for

industrial development. It is aligned to the Kenya Vision 2030 which advocates for making education responsive to educational

needs. Metalwork is also in line with Sessional Paper No 1 of 2019 which recommends the promotion of technical and vocational

education with an emphasis on Science, Technology, and Innovation (ST&I) in the school curriculum.

Upon completing senior school, learners may advance by enrolling in either a tertiary institution or university to further their

studies in engineering or technology-based courses. Alternatively, they can join related career opportunities on salaried or self-

employment terms. Metalwork offers a broad range of career opportunities across industries like manufacturing, construction,

automotive, aerospace, art, and jewelry. These careers can be technical, creative, or managerial, depending on the skills and int

GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior Secondary, the learner should be able to: -

1. Attain a firm foundation for the study of Metalwork, further training, and education.

2. Use knowledge and skills in drawing to design items that can be made using metals.

3. Use metals to fabricate items that can be used to solve problems in the society.

4. Correctly select and use metal working tools and equipment for given tasks.

5. Carry out metal joining using the various metal joining processes.

6. Use acquired competencies in identifying business opportunity, set up, and ethically run an enterprise in metal working related

field.

7. Prudently manage finances and create wealth using metallic materials.

8. Appreciate Metalwork in technical and social economic development of the country.

9. Promote national and international consciousness fostering positive attitudes toward other people and nations.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

Kenya’s people belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able

to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by

resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect which enable them to live together in harmony and foster

patriotism in order to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution following in the wake of rapid

modernization. Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and

relevant domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

ii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instill in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will

lead to physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It

should lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iii

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre-

career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Power Mechanics as a subject builds upon the competencies acquired in Pre-Technical studies at Junior School. At this level,

learners will deepen their understanding of mechanical principles, power systems and practical applications moving from basic

concepts to more complex and specialized ones.

The subject covers key content areas including; Fundamentals of power mechanics, Related drawing, Vehicle systems and Engines.

The transition emphasises enhanced critical thinking, problem-solving, and hands-on skills that prepare learners for real-world

technical challenges. Learners are expected to develop the core competencies and values outlined in the Basic Education

curriculum Framework (BECF). Pertinent and contemporary issues (PCIs) such as social economic and environmental issues and

citizenship education and are mainstreamed in the learning experiences. Learning at this level is learner cantered and formative

assessment emphasised.

Upon completion of Senior School, competencies gained by learners in this subject will enable them transit into various post-

secondary tertiary institutions such as Universities, National polytechnics, technical training institutes, Technical and vocational

centres or transit to the world of work.

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. attain a firm foundation for career growth, further training and education in power mechanics related areas of study;

2. utilise acquired power mechanics competencies to service and repair motor vehicle systems;

3. apply acquired drawing skills to interpret and communicate engineering designs using information and communication

technology where applicable;

4. relate positively with members of the society during visits to work environment;

5. use acquired knowledge to identify business opportunities related to power mechanics;

6. appreciate the place of power mechanics in day-to-day life.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

Kenya’s people belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able

to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by

resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect which enable them to live together in harmony and foster

patriotism in order to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth

progress of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution following in the wake of

rapid modernization. Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and

relevant domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya

recognizes the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be

part of this development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will

prepare our young people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

ii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead

to physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should

lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iii

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre-

career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Woodwork is an optional subject offered at the senior school level, specifically within the Technical Studies track of the STEM

pathway. It builds upon the competencies acquired during Pre-Technical Studies in junior school. The subject equips learners with

the foundational knowledge, skills, attitudes, and values necessary to specialize in Technical Studies at the senior school level.

The subject focuses on the processing of timber and related products to create useful items for society, allowing learners to explore

the unique relationship between trees, wood products, and humanity. It emphasizes the sustainable use and management of wood

as a vital natural resource, essential for addressing the challenges of the 21st century. Wood serves as a fundamental material in

woodwork, valued for its beauty, durability, workability, and sustainability, making it ideal for creating both functional and artistic

objects in construction and various crafts. The subject maintains a balance between theoretical and practical work, engaging

learners in projects that connect the content to their local environment. It fosters exploration, imagination, creativity, and

innovation through hands-on projects and practical activities. Learners also gain practical experience by participating in industrial

attachment programs facilitated through partnerships between schools and industry.

The curriculum is structured into four strands: Foundations of Woodwork, Materials, Timber Processes and Products, and Related

Drawing, spanning Grades 10 to 12. Through this structure, learners acquire the knowledge, skills, attitudes, and values necessary

for further training in tertiary institutions or for direct entry into the workforce through apprenticeships. They are prepared to

pursue careers in fields such as wood science, carpentry and joinery, building construction, manufacturing, among others

vii

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of senior school, the learner should be able to:

1. Acquire knowledge on career opportunities, employability, and entrepreneurial skills in Woodwork.

2. Practice proper health and safety measures in the woodworking workplace

3. Demonstrate skills in identifying, selecting, using, and maintaining woodworking tools, machines, and equipment in the

workplace.

4. Apply acquired skills in the production, processing, storage, selection, and utilisation of timber and other materials for effective

use in woodworking.

5. Identify and utilise available timber for the production of timber products.

6. Use technical drawing skills as a communication tool for planning and designing woodworking products

7. Demonstrate creativity, innovation, and skill in finishing wood products.

8. Appreciate the benefits of evolution of technology and its application in Woodwork
